title: What Stands Owed on a Rider at the Moment of Closure
content:
What stands owed on one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders as it is closed is taken from one of two places, according to the rider's standing.

## The rule

**Where the rider stands suspended for unpaid premium**, what stands owed is the figure the rider record shows standing owed.

**Where the rider stands ended**, nothing stands owed.

**Otherwise**, what stands owed is what every charge on the rider premium account comes to less every payment and every credit on it.

## Condition and amount

| The rider's standing | What stands owed |
|---|---|
| Suspended for unpaid premium | The figure the rider record shows standing owed |
| Ended | Nothing |
| Any other standing | Every charge on the account, less every payment and every credit on it |

In the third case the amount is rounded to the nearest cent and is never less than nothing.

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

A rider premium account carries charges coming to 184.50 USD, payments coming to 61.50 USD and credits coming to 12.00 USD, while the rider record shows 98.00 USD standing owed.

- **Suspended for unpaid premium:** what stands owed is 98.00 USD, the figure the record shows.
- **Ended:** nothing stands owed.
- **Any other standing:** what stands owed is 184.50 USD less 61.50 USD less 12.00 USD, that is 111.00 USD.

Where the entries came to less than nothing between them, the third case would give nothing rather than a negative figure.
